anomaly_def.Name: Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Replication Synchronization Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : Excessive growth of buffer caches, work areas, or other engine heaps drives the host into sustained memory pressure.
Replication Synchronization Anomaly : Stand-by or downstream replicas cannot receive or apply the primary’s transaction log fast enough, causing widening replication lag.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes consume most or all available CPU cycles, saturating the host scheduler.

When all three root causes occur together the system exhibits an intertwined failure pattern: memory pressure triggers paging and stalls, while CPU saturation lengthens every critical path—foreground queries, background check-pointers, and replica receiver / applier threads alike. Replica apply lag widens rapidly, retaining ever-larger log segments on the primary; these segments increase both disk and in-memory metadata footprints, aggravating the already tight memory envelope. Operators may observe "run-queue" and "memory-pressure" wait events simultaneously, soaring context-switch rates, growing WAL/redo queues, expanding plan and buffer eviction churn, and replicas drifting so far behind that read scalability and fail-over readiness collapse.

Causal chain: (1) Heavy workload or run-away operations inflate per-session work areas and caches, pushing the engine beyond safe RAM limits and causing OS paging; (2) paging and cache churn escalate CPU demand as the engine repeatedly faults and re-loads pages; (3) with CPU now saturated, replication receiver and applier threads are de-scheduled more frequently and replay throughput drops; (4) falling replay throughput forces the primary to retain more log segments and in-memory replication state, further swelling memory usage and intensifying pressure; (5) this positive feedback loop amplifies latency across the whole workload and risks OOM kills, primary node eviction, or replica divergence. The mutual reinforcement of memory exhaustion, CPU starvation, and replication backlog makes the composite anomaly harder to diagnose than any single component defect.

entry.official_definition: The time limit for regular expression matching operations performed by the regular expression engine.
entry.trigger_condition: A regular expression match operation exceeds regexp_time_limit.
entry.workload_impact: The regular expression operation is constrained by the configured time limit.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
